newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists appeal on immigrants law.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists appeal on immigrants law.

text.p: France's opposition Socialists appealed to the Constitutional Council on Thursday in an attempt to have a hotly-disputed law clamping down on illegal immigration thrown out.

The Socialist Party said its deputies and senators had protested to the watchdog body against measures including a national register of French citizens and their foreign guests and the taking of fingerprints of anyone applying for a residence permit.

The latter "allows the Interior Ministry to have access to records of asylum-seekers...which seriously threatens the legal security of those placed under our country's protection", the party said in a statement.

The bill had prompted widespread protests by artists, intellectuals and leftist parties which had pledged to ask the Council to check whether the law conforms to the constitution, the country's top legal chart.

The law introduces articles to immigration regulations that will allow police to keep passports or travel documents of illegal immigrants, who are said by authorities to often destroy their documents to avoid being sent home.

France's biggest opposition force said the law, which got final approval by the Senate on Wednesday, threatened to create a new category of immigrants bereft of residence status and gave authority to prefects (government representatives) rather than judges to define clandestine labour.

"All these provisions are a serious attack on the individual liberty of French and foreign nationals, on the rights of the defence, on the duties of the judicial authority and on the equality of treatment between citizens," the party said.
The Interior Ministry said 36 Romanians who had either entered the country illegally or contravened public order laws were flown home to Bucharest aboard a government-chartered aircraft on Thursday.

It was the 39th such collective deportation of illegal immigrants since conservative President Jacques Chirac came to power in May 1995, taking the number of foreigners expelled in that period to 23,559.
